full_judgment:
56. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Advocate with Syed Mokaddes Ali, learned Advocate appearing for the appellant submits that in order to grab the suit property the founder of Eastern Housing Ltd, late Mr. Jahurul Islam discovered so called Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157 Baro Moghbazar, who is not real Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, he did not pay any installments for the plot which was allotted by DIT in favour of this defendant No. 3, who is Executive Engineer, C&B department. Defendant No. 3 paid the installments on different dates following the rules of RAJUK in the National Bank of Pakistan at the then Jinnah Avenue Branch and he has receipts showing such payments. Learned Advocate further submits that as per plaint the date of delivery of possession and the date of registration of the lease deed are the same which clearly show the fraudulent activities of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157 Baro Moghbazar. Learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiffs claimed their father was an engineer in C&B department and he had house of his own comprising 10 kathas of land at 157, Baro Moghbazar as such it is not believable that an Executive Engineer of C&B will leave such a coveted post to join the company, of Mr. Zahurul Islam. Learned Advocate further submits that defendant No. 3-appellant as the real Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, joined the then C&B Department as Assistant Engineer and after long service was promoted to the post of Executive Engineer and his name and particulars of his service are available in Government records. On his application while he was in service the then DIT allotted the suit plot with him and he paid all installments and possession was delivered to him and the lease deed was registered in his favour on 1-8-1962, he mutated his name, paid municipal taxes, water, electricity and gas bills and was in peaceful possession of the suit property. Learned Advocate further submits that the father of the plaintiffs i.e. so called Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza and another so-called Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza both are fake created persons of Eastern Housing Ltd only to grab the suit property who used the name of this defendant No. 3-appellant. Learned Advocate further submits that, after the plot was allotted to this defendant No. 3 vide letter No. 2409 dated 21-3-1962 and the defendant No. 3-appellant having paid full value of the plot by installments as fixed, RAJUK delivered possession of the suit plot to him, thereafter standard lease agreement was executed and registered in his favour on 1-8-1962 being deed No. 7198 and he became the 16 armas owner of the suit plot, this defendant No. 3-appellant got mutation khatian and got his name recorded in the City Corporation, electricity, WASA and Titas gas department and continued to possess the suit land by paying rents, taxes and bills for the said plot and in the last settlement operation, RS and Mohanagar Survey, his name has been correctly recorded and thereafter, this defendant No.3 applied on 25-1-1966 for permission to make construction on the suit plot and RAJUK by memo No. 4452 dated 29-10-1966 granted permission to construct two storied building. And he made construction and continued to live in the suit property and later he having need of money, entered into an agreement for sale of the suit holding with defendant No. 4, MNH Bhulu at a consideration of Tk. 2,35,00,000 and on receipt of Tk. 5,00,000 executed a bainapatra on 18-1-2004 and thereafter defendant No. 3 filed application on 18-2-2004 to RAJUK for sale permission but RAJUK did not pay any heed to it, then he sent 4 legal notices through his advocate on 20-4-2004 to defendant Nos. 5 to 8 and RAJUK received the same on 22-4-2004 but did not give any reply as such he filed Title Suit No. 176 of 2004 on 31-5-2004 and the RAJUK as defendants though received summons but did not file any written statements for long time and when the suit was fixed for exparte hearing, RAJUK filed written statement on 8-3-2006 and contesting the suit. Defendant No.3 applied to Parliamentary Standing Committee to get possession of the suit building and the Standing Committee constituted a sub-committee with the Chairman RAJUK as member secretary, This defendant No.3 himself appeared before the committee on 28-7-2004 and gave statement before the committee but the plaintiffs or their representative did not appear before the committee, None also appeared on behalf of the defendant No-1. The committee after hearing decided that applicant was government officer, RAJUK would obtain information relating to his service from the concerned department and will inform the committee about the progress in respect of its decision. On 16-9-2004 the Secretary RAJUK requested the relevant section of the Ministry of Communication to send information relating to the service of the defendant No.3 then the Superintendent Engineer of Accounts  Department of Road and High Ways sent the report including photo on 5-3-2005 from which it appears that defendant No.3 was appointed in C&B Design Division-1 under Ministry of Communication on 19-8-1952 and joined in Project Circle-2, Dhaka as Assistant Engineer and on 19-7-1960 was promoted to the post of Executive Engineer Design Section and Building Project Circle, C&B. The report showes that there is account for withdrawal of salary and allowances till 18-8-1963 and his residential address was mentioned as 7-75, Railway Colony, Babu Para, lswardi, Patina photo attached'. From all these facts, Learned Advocate submits that this defendant No.3 is the real Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, plaintiffs and defendant No.1 through fraudulent means are trying to grab the property lawfully owned by defendant No.3, who is the real owner i.e. defendant No. 3 who is not the father of the plaintiffs and they are not sons and daughters of defendant No. 3. Defendant No. 3-appellant did not execute anv agreement with any one except defendant No. 4. Learned Advocate further submits that this defendant No.3 deposed in Title Suit No. 176 of 2004 as PW l which was illegally adopted in Title Suit No. 81 of 2006 though the cause of action of two suits are different. Learned Advocate further submits that defendant No. 3 by oral as well as by exhibits proved his case and exhibits having been entered into evidence without any objection cannot be challenged later on, these exhibits proved that he is real Shamsul Kabir Hu.mayun ReLZ in whose favour the suit plot was allotted, Learned Advocate on reference to the deposition of PW 1, Nasiruddin Khan of Title Suit No. 81 of 2006 and on reference to the written statement filed by defendant Nos. 5 to 8, RAJUK in Title Suit No. 81 of 2006 and on reference to Order VIII of the Code of Civil Procedure submits that there is no provision for cancelling one written statement by another and further submits that there is provision for amendment of written statement but such amendment cannot change the fundamental character of the defence and such amendment which change the character of written state-ment is riot legally acceptable, so the subsequent written statement filed by RAJUK is not legally acceptable and does not deserve any consideration. Learned Advocate here relied on the decisions of 27 DLR (AD) 114 paragraph 5 and 14 BLD 61 paragraph 1.0, Learned Advocate on reference to section 169 of Town Improvement Act, 1953 submits that, statutory notice as required to be issued under section 169 of the Town Improvement Act, 1953 has not been delivered or left at RAJUK office nor the plaint contains a statement that such notice has been delivered as such the instant suit is liable to be dismissed as it does not fulfill the legal requirements. Learned Advocate here refer to the decisions of 41 DLR 332, 21 BLD 565. Learned Advocate on reference to the deposition of DW 4, Abu Bakkar Siddique in Title Suit No.176 of 2004, submits that, in cross-examination this witness admitted that he is not authorized to depose on behalf of RAJUK as such his evidence is inadmissible. Learned Advocate thereafter submits that learned Joint District Judge illegally observed on the Matriculation and Intermediate certificates of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza although produced in Court and marked as exhibit 4, but did not consider the Matriculation and Intermediate certificates as the father's name of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza i.e. this defendant have not been mentioned as such the observation given is not based on proper appreciation of materials on record further submits that and there is no evidence that these certificates were awarded to Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, who is the predecessor of the plaintiffs residing at 157, Baro Moghbazar, Dhaka. Learned Advocate then submits that the observation of the learned Judge that a Diploma Engineer can never be appointed as Assistant Engineer in C&B department is not a proper observation. Learned Advocate further submits that, the finding of the learned Judge that plaintiff of Title Suit No. 176 of 2004 and defendant No. 3 of Title Suit No. 81 of 2006 is not Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, who was allotted the plot is not the owner of the suit property but plaintiff's father of Title Suit No.81 of 2006 is owner of the suit property but before arriving at this finding the learned Subordinate Judge did not consider the papers filed by the defendant No. 3-appellant in Title Suit No. 176 of 2004 and these exhibits were entered into evidence without any objection as such these exhibits have legal presumptive value and refer to the decision of 44 DLR (AD) 162. Learned Advocate further submits that the finding of the learned Judge that Diploma Engineer can never be appointed as Assistant Engineer in C&B which is illegal, baseless and arrived on conjecture and surmises and as such this finding of the trial Court is perverse. Here the learned Advocate refers to the decision of 8 MLR (AD) 217 paragraph 14 where it has been held that Diploma Engineer who was appointed Sub-Assistant Engineer was promoted to the post of Executive Engineer of Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation, a statutory body. Learned Advocate further submits that adopted depositions of witnesses in 3 suits i.e. Title Suit No. 51 of 2004, Title Suit No. 176 of 2004 and Title Suit No. 81 of 2004 according to section 33 of the Evidence Act, 1872 is not proper as all these suits are filed separately and on different cause of action and refer to the decision of 11 DLR (SC) 38, 10 DLR (SC) 193. 

 59. Now turned to the plaintiff's documents, it appears that plaintiffs filed allotment letter, exhibit 1. General Power of Attorney by the heirs of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157 of Baro Mogbazar exhibits 2, 3, 3ka in favour of Eastern Housing Ltd, Matriculation certificate of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157 Baro Mogbazar, exhibit 4, Intermediate Certificate of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Baro Mogbazar, exhibt 4ka. BA Engineering Certificate Part 11 of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, of 157, Baro Moghbazar, exhibit 4kha, BA Engineering Certificate of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, of 157 Baro Moghbazar, exhibit 4 ga. Pakistani Domicile Declaration of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, exhibit 5. Deed of sale executed in favour of AZM Sanaullah dated 24-9-1957, exhibit 6. Deed of sale executed by A.Z.M. Sanaullah dated 24-9-1957 in favour of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza in respect of the property at Baro Mogbazar, then Heba deed executed by Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza in favour of his wife, Selima Begum dated 17-8-1979 as exhibit 7, approved plan of DIT as exhibit 8, voter identity card of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza exhibit 9, Passport of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza as exhibit 9ka. Certificate issued by the Government of Canada in favour of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza as exhibit 10, Promotion letter, exhibits 11 series, allotment letter of DIT in favour of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza as exhibit 12, deposite receipts showing payment of installments as exhibits 12ka to 13gha, Exhibits 13 uma to 13 chha are the letter of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157 Baro Mogbazar to DIT informing payment of installments. Exhibit 14 is handing over possession with letter to Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza for depositing Tk.51, Exhibit . 15 is standard lease deed of DIT, Exhibit 16 letter of DIT approving plan, Exhibit 16 ka is photocopy of DIT. approved plan, Letter of House Building Finance Corporation for loan as exhibit 17. Exhibit 17ka is mortgaged deed between Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157 Baro Moghbazar and House Building Finance Corporation, Exhibits 18 series are the tenancy agreement with Agency for International deve-lopment, USA. Tenancy agreement showing that disputed plot was given in rent to different agencies from 1967 upto 2000. Exhibits 19 series are letters of WASA for water connection showing payment of gas, electricity and WASA bills, Exhibit 20 is municipal assessment tax for 1967 to 1968, Exhibit 20ka is municipal assessment tax for 1968 to 1969, Exhibit 20kha is the city corporation holding tax 2003 to 2004, Exhibits 21- 21na series  are government land tax, Exhibit 22 is RS khatian No.1174, Exhibits 23 - 23ka series are Memorandum and Articles of Association of Bengal Development Corporation Ltd, Exhibits 24-24uma series yearly audit report of Uttara Bank Ltd. 1996-2001, Exhibit 25 is the letter of DIT regarding fees for changing plot from residential to commercial, Exhibit 26 is Permission letter of RAJUK, Exhibit 27 is general power of attorney executed by Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza in favour of Eastern Housing Ltd, Exhibit 28 is approval letter RAJUK, Exhibits 29 - 29kha series are approved plan, Exhibits 30-30 Oa series warning published in newspaper, Exhibits 31-31Ka series corrigendum published in Daily Janakantha, Exhibit 32 is death certificate of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, Exhibit 33 is news published in different news papers by the Uttara Bank on the death of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, Exhibit 33ka is succession certificate issued by the Ward Commissioner of Ward No. 53, Exhibit 34 is succession certificate issued by the District Judge, Dhaka. Exhibit 35 is plaint of Title Suit No. 51 of 2004, Exhibit 36 is plaint of Title Suit No. 176 of 2004, Exhibit 37 to 37ka series are pay bills, Exhibit 38 passport No. B-57985 of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza. 

 62. Now to FA No. 327 of 2009. Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza filed Title Suit No. 176 of 2004 giving his address as plot No. 34, present 113, Block No-CWN(B), Gulshan Model Town, PS Gulshan, District Dhaka against DIT's officials praying for pass a decree in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants declaring that the defendants are bound to dispose of the application dated 18-2-2004 filed by the plaintiff for sale permission in respect of the scheduled property by the Court by receiving the proper transfer fees as per rule of RAJUK. It is the case of the plaintiff that the suit property originally belonged to RAJUK, it was allotted to the plaintiff by defendants and plaintiff by successive four installments from 26-3-1962 up to 3-2-1965 paid the installments and after observing all the formalities of DIT, who having satisfied, executed and registered the standard lease agreement deed in favour of the plaintiff being Deed No. 7198 dated 1-8-11972 in the office of the sadar Sub-Registry, Dhaka. The suit property was delivered to the plaintiff. Plaintiff acquired full right, title, interest and possession over the suit property. Plaintiff mutated his name and paid municipality, WASA, electricity and titas gas bills regularly. After getting connection from different authorities plaintiff's name has been recorded in RS khatian and also mohanagar settlement and after acquiring all sorts of ownership plaintiff seeking permission for construction over the schedule property on 25-1-1966 and permission was given for construction work under office memo No. 4452 dated 29-10-1966. Plaintiff further stated that he completed two storied building, residing and enjoying the property by himself and through the tenants. Plaintiff thereafter in dire need of urgent cash money, entered into an agreement/bainanama with MNH Bhulu on 18-1-2004 at a consideration of amount of Tk. 2,35,00,000 and received Taka 5,00,000 as earnest money from him. Thereafter plaintiff applied to defendant No. 4 on 18-2-2004 to accord for necessary sale per-mission but that has not been done so several legal notices were served. Thereafter, plaintiff filed the aforesaid suit. 

 111. P. W. No. 1 claiming as Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza in his deposition has stated that he the Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza got, the allopient from Rajuk in the year 1962. Allotment letter being No. 2409 dated 21- 37,1962  produced before the Court and marked as exhibit 1. He has paid the entire lease many vide four receipts through National Bank of Pakistan which have been produced in the Court and marked as exhibit 2, 2 (ka), 2 (kha) and 2 (Ga) dated 26-2-62, 15-5-63, 15-5-64 and 546 respectively. He got the possession of the lease plot from, Rajuk. Possession hand over letter' dated 7-4-62 produced before the Court and larked as exhibit -3- Rajuk executed the lease deed and registered the same on 1-8-1962 being deed No.7198 which was produced and marked as exhibit 4. Exhibit 5 is the security money receipt of Tk-500/=. On an application plaintiff approved the plan from Rajuk being No. 4452 dated 29-10-1966 which is exhibit "6". Rajuk vide letter 4452 dated 29-10-2006 permitted plaintiff to construct the building which was produced before the Court and marked as Exhibit-7. Suit plot has been mutated in the name of the plaintiff and paid the rent those were produced before the Court and marked as exhibit 8, 8 (ka) and 8 (kha). Revisional survey record was prepared and published in the name of the plaintiff and khatian No. 1174 has been prepared in his name produced and marked as exhibit 9. Mahanagar record was prepared provisionally in the name of plaintiff. Plaintiff made an agreement with N.H. Bhulu for selling the suit property and prayed for sale permission on 18-2-2004. Rajuk did not accord permission nor refused the application for sale permission. Therefore, plaintiff on 20-4-2004 served a legal notice upon Rajuk by registered post with A/D which was received by the Rajuk, the copies of Registered A/D produced before Court and marked as exhibit 10 series. 

 112. In cross examination he has stated and admitted that he has passed the Diploma thereafter he did not obtain any decree. He admitted that in his letter of allotment name of the allottee has been written Humayun Reza but he did not object it. He admitted that at the time of bainanama he was in Geneva Camp, Syedpur. Later told he was not in Geneva Camp and does not know the name of in charge of Geneva camp. He did not produce the domicile certificate. His correspondence address is 154 Moghbazar which has been written in the allotment letter. He admitted that address 157 Bara Moghbazar has been written in the RS Khatian. However, he is not the resident of 157 Bara Moghbazar. He admitted that in Exhibit 7 address has been written 157 Bara Moghbazar not 154 Moghbazar. It is not a fact that RS Khatian has not been written in his name but in the name of Shamsul Karim Humayun Reza of 157 Bara Moghbazar. He could not say who resides in 157 Bara Moghbazar. He admitted that there is no seal in his passport that he went to India in 1958. He did not take retirement but resigned from the service. He had no service book. He stated that at that time he has lacs of money. Later stated he has paid the installment of Tk. 20,000 taking loan from his relative. At that time personally he had no money. He has no bank account. He admitted that at present value of 1 Katha is taka one crore. At first he admitted but later denied that since he is not the owner of the land for that reason he has created Bainanama of 2,35,00,000 in place of 20 crore. He admitted that he did not show the Tk. 5,00,000 in income tax file. He has no TIN. He admitted that he could not say in what paragraph of the plaint he has stated that he was in the suit plot in 1971. He admitted that since there is no statement in the plaint that is why he could not say. His son and brother-in-law died in the suit plot in 1971. However, he did not file any murder case but made a GD entry. He admitted that he could not say date and number of GD entry. He further admitted that he could not produce the copy of GD entry. He admitted that exhibit 4 lease deed No. 7198 but in plaint deed number has been written 1198 dated 1-8-1962. He stated that he was executive engineer but could not understand the ACR and Organogram.
